flags: PARTIAL OVERVIEW: both NCDOT guidebook cache files contain identical text truncated in the Flat Rock chapter, before Airlie Road. Their page-fragment URLs do not supply those pages. The table of contents confirms byway inclusion only; route-specific designation rationale, road character and history remain unsupported.

Dropped unsupported current claims: US 76/Military Cutoff start, 1.5-mile length, pine and Spanish-moss oak canopy, sudden opening to marsh grass and docks, drawbridge endpoint, five-minute drive, and the road being named for the gardens. Catalog and current text cannot replace the missing cache chapter.

Overview is shorter and uses regional access history, not an assertion that Shell Road is Airlie Road. Stop order follows material; exact byway endpoints cannot be established. Wrightsville Beach is retained as the onward town, not a claimed byway endpoint.
Garden creation dates conflict: 02 gives 1886; 08 gives 1901; 10 says early 1900s. Omitted the current 1886 date pending stronger evidence.
Airlie Oak’s 2007 measurements and ranking are dated, not presented as a current ranking. Omitted the age of 500 years rather than add the current draft’s unsourced hedge “reckoned.”

Evans article contradicts its 1974 retirement with “for the rest of her life”; used explicit retirement date. It also dates an artwork after her death; that claim is not reused. Wrightsville article has conflicting streetcar end dates, omitted.
No current site-manager cache verifies visitor arrangements; hours and admission promises are omitted.
